_comment: Presentation. ALL of it is TUNABLE and none of it is a mechanic. The expected feedback is 'too dark', 'the grass is the wrong green', 'the creatures don't move enough' — every one of those has to be answerable by editing this file rather than by editing a scene.
_comment_scale: Nothing here sets a collider or a hit range. Art is fitted to the gameplay size the species and the controller already declare; if a value in this file could change how far an attack reaches, it is in the wrong file.

trainer._comment_height: Metres, matched to the CharacterBody3D capsule in scenes/player/player.tscn. The model is measured and scaled to this, so a replacement of any size drops in without touching the scene.
trainer._comment_yaw: Degrees of correction for which way the source model faces. Verified from a survey frame, not assumed — there is no convention across asset packs.
trainer._comment_clips: Five clips, authored by tools/art_pipeline/blender/animate_humanoid.py and baked into the .glb, so the role and the clip name are the same string and nothing is retargeted. They are procedural cycles, not hand-animated character work — the first thing to upgrade.
trainer._comment_libraries: Empty now, and kept as a key because the merge path still works. KayKit's Ranger needed it: that character ships a rig with zero clips and the motion in shared libraries. This model carries its own clips. Its skeleton is also NOT KayKit's — KayKit's character is about two heads tall and sheet 04's trainer is 6.25, so neither the weights nor the clips transfer between them.
trainer._comment_model: Sheet 04's trainer, produced through tools/art_pipeline. The body and the head were generated separately and grafted: nine whole-figure candidates across three rounds all came back with a blank ovoid for a face, because at a 30k budget spread over a standing figure an eye socket is smaller than the triangles available to describe it.

sky._comment: Mid-morning, high summer, clear. Taken from the key art board rather than invented: a warm low-contrast sky over saturated grass is most of what makes the reference read as inviting rather than as a tech demo.
sky._comment_panorama: An HDRI panorama, when the time of day names one. The procedural gradient below is the FALLBACK and stays because a missing texture should degrade to the old sky rather than to a black void. The critic measured the procedural sky's horizontal variation at 0.020 against Palworld's 0.140-0.289 and said the build sky 'contributes nothing' — a ProceduralSkyMaterial can make a vertical gradient and a soft sun blob and nothing else, ever. No amount of tuning puts a cloud in it.

sun._comment: One directional light. `pitch` well above the horizon so shadows are short and readable under a top-down-ish combat camera; long raking shadows look dramatic in a screenshot and hide the opponent in a fight.
sun._comment_shadow: Normal bias fights the acne that a heightmap terrain produces at grazing angles. Raise it if the ground looks striped; lower it if small props stop casting.
sun._comment_energy: Bright. The first pass at real lighting overshot into gloom: the arena went near-black and the creatures stopped being readable, which is a worse failure than the flat lighting it replaced. Value RANGE was the goal — bright sun, real shadows — not darkness.
sun._comment_pitch_r9_4: R9.4. Was -52. The blind critic found frames 01-04 'effectively flat-lit' -- boosting contrast 3x revealed almost no terrain form -- while frame 05, the only low-sun frame, was 'by a wide margin the best-lit frame in the set' and the only one whose value statistics land inside the references' range. Dropped to -44 rather than to 05's -13: the original comment's reason for a high sun is real (long raking shadows hide the opponent under a top-down-ish combat camera) and this keeps shadows short while giving slopes a lit and a shaded side. TUNABLE, and the thing to re-check first if combat readability regresses.

environment._comment: Tonemap and fog. ACES holds highlights on sunlit grass instead of clipping them to white, which was the single worst thing about the previous prototype's look.
environment._comment_fog: Very light, and warm rather than grey. It exists to separate near hills from far ones; at any strength where you notice it as fog, it is too strong.
environment._comment_fog_measured: Halved from 0.0022. At the old density the blind critic measured `03-rise-overlook` at mean saturation 0.235 against 0.51 for a frame in the same biome, and said fog was 'eating the world rather than describing depth' — every object past ~150m a grey stamp. The reference does the same job with comparable haze and keeps a saturated tree band in front of it, so the fix is less fog, not less distance.
environment._comment_ambient: Sky ambient with a real colour underneath it. `sky_contribution` blends between the two. Quadrupling ambient energy with pure sky ambient moved the survey frames by NOTHING — sky radiance does not reach the terrain under the Compatibility renderer the harness is forced to use — while an explicit colour lifted the shaded ground by 55%. Specifying both means shaded ground is filled under either renderer, and 'shadows are filled by this much of this colour' is a decision somebody made rather than a side effect of a procedural sky.
environment._comment_ambient_r9_4: R9.4. Was 1.25. High ambient is what removed the bottom of the value range: the critic measured the 5th-percentile luminance of frames 01 and 03 at 126 and 117 -- the DARKEST 5% of those images was still a mid-tone -- against 17 for palworld-04, and luminance standard deviation at 28-36 against the references' 52-69. Ambient light with nowhere to fall off is a flat frame by construction. Cut to 0.95, not lower: this file already records one pass that overshot into gloom and made the arena unreadable, and the ground albedo itself now carries most of the value drop (see terrain_playground's grass tint). TUNABLE.
environment._comment_fog_r9_4: R9.4. Halved again, 0.0011 -> 0.00055, and the colour warmed off neutral grey. The critic: 'fog is eating the world, not describing it' -- everything past the mid-ground washing to one pale value with no separation between hills, against palworld-04 which keeps three readable value planes at distance. It also produced the survey's most-reported inconsistency: frames 03 and 04 appear to have a flat cream sky, which is not sky at all but fogged-out terrain filling the upper frame, so two viewpoints of the same place look like different biomes. Less fog, not less distance. TUNABLE.

_comment_times: Named hours. Each states ONLY what it changes; everything else comes from the blocks above. `hour` (0-24) is when scripts/world/day_cycle.gd treats this as the active preset -- see R5.1.
_comment_times_why: The previous survey shipped a frame called `05-spawn-low-sun` whose sky was BIT-IDENTICAL to the midday frame beside it — 46.8% of the image pixel-for-pixel the same — because dropping the sun meant rotating a DirectionalLight3D and nothing else. The sun disc, sky gradient, horizon haze and fog all stayed at noon. The key art board asks for 'day and night create different moods'; a sky that does not move with the sun cannot give one. So the hour is one value and everything derives from it. Nothing should reach for the Sun node directly again.
_comment_day_cycle: TUNABLE (CLAUDE.md 'Tunable Values'): how fast the clock runs and when the world counts as genuinely dark, for scripts/world/day_cycle.gd. No gameplay reads these yet -- R5.1 is presentation only, matching GAME_DESIGN.md 24's 'do not just add levels to every pal at night'; nocturnal spawn rules are a later, separate decision.

day._comment: Mid-morning, high summer, clear. The default, and what the biome is designed around.

golden._comment: Late afternoon. Long shadows, warm key, the sky's blue pushed down and the horizon lifted to amber. This is the mood the key art's own sunset panel is selling, and it is the one hour where the meadow gets its warm end of the palette for free.

night._comment: No panorama exists for this yet (only day.hdr/golden.hdr were generated), so it falls back to the procedural gradient on purpose -- a missing texture degrading to the old sky beats a black void. The sun stands in for moonlight: low energy, cool, low in the sky rather than below the horizon so there is still one soft shadow direction to read.

sky._comment_panorama: Explicitly empty. The base `sky` block above names day.hdr; _merged() layers this dict on top of that one, so without this the night preset would silently inherit the DAY panorama instead of falling back to the procedural gradient.

_comment_creature_motion_removed: The procedural bob that used to be configured here is gone. The creatures are rigged and animated now, so they have real idle, walk, run, attack and death clips — faking motion on top of that would fight the animation.

grandpa._comment: Grandpa Elias. He stands where he is put and talks — beat 3 of docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md — so `idle` is the only clip he needs today. The other four ship with him because they cost nothing to author on the same skeleton and he will eventually walk.
grandpa._comment_height: Shorter than the 1.8m trainer. He is an old man and the silhouette should say so before the dialogue does.

villager_farmer._comment: R7.2. Grandpa's own rig and clips, tinted rather than regenerated — see character_model.gd's `_apply_tint` comment for why this is the model reused (Ranger is stylistically incompatible, and CLAUDE.md forbids pre-empting the open art-pipeline question in ralph/BLOCKED.md by using it anyway). `tint` multiplies every surface's existing albedo, so the texture detail survives and only the hue/value shifts — a rustier, warmer wardrobe than Grandpa's own.

villager_keeper._comment: R7.2. Same tinting approach as villager_farmer, on the trainer's rig instead of Grandpa's — a second silhouette so the square does not read as three copies of one man. Cooler, greener tint keeps it visually apart from both the trainer (the player's own body) and villager_farmer.

villager_smith._comment: R7.2. Trainer rig again, a third tint — the well square gets a farmer, a keeper and a smith without a third model.

warden._comment: The Warden of the Meadows, the biome's final boss. Board 06 used directly, per the owner lifting the earlier override (docs/art/REFERENCE_CANON.md). He does not appear in the first fifteen minutes; he is here so the biome's end is not a stand-in.
warden._comment_face: His face is a painted mask, not modelled features. That is the art, not a shortcut: board 06 masks him, and asking the generator for a hard visor plays to what it can actually do after nine whole-figure candidates came back with blank ovoids.
